symptom: ako/mxcli#1930 (mendixlabs/mxcli#1728): a validation decision (`if trim($X/Code) != '' then else set $Valid = false; end if;`) is described folded, `if not(trim($X/Code) != '') then set $Valid = false; end if;`. Feeding that description back through `create or modify microflow` with only the condition text changed stored `not(trim($X/Reference) != '')` as the decision's expression while its true/false flows stayed: the decision was inverted, and check --references, exec ("spliced: 1 edited in place") and diff all looked harmless.
cause: describe's empty-then swap (true path straight to the merge, false path with content) prints negateIfCondition(expr) and swaps the paths, but the splice's in-place condition edit (patchDiff.conditionEdit → splitCondition → SetCondition, ako/mxcli#888) stored the script's condition text as it was. The flows are untouched by a condition edit, so the printed negation went into the model un-negated.
file: mdl/executor/cmd_alter_flow.go (splitCondition negates when decisionPrintedNegated), mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_show_helpers.go (negateExpression extracted from negateIfCondition; decisionPrintedNegated recomputes describe's fold from the stored flows with findSplitMergePoints + findBranchFlows)
insight: A describer that rewrites what it prints (here: negate and swap for readability) creates an obligation on every path that reads its output back: the inverse transform. Decide the fold from the stored flows with describe's own merge computation, never from the text — describe also strips a stored not(Z) to Z, so 'the printed condition starts with not(' detects neither case reliably. negateExpression is its own inverse, which is what makes the round trip exact: printed not(Y) stores Y, printed Z stores not(Z). Test: create the reporter's flow on a pedapp copy, describe, change only the attribute in the printed condition, exec under mdl 1; assert the decision kept its $ID and stores the un-negated expression, for both fold shapes; with the negation stubbed both fail with the inversion. A decision in a loop body is not edited at all (the splice refuses), pinned by a second test.
